body:
I'm particularly interested in feedback from

- @passivestar 
- @Calinou 
- @migueldeicaza 
- @bruvzg 

Any anyone else who uses macOS.

Hi, please note that these gestures are not only exposed by MacOS but also Wayland, which is now unusable.

MacOS says that the unit used is points per second, so I think that it'd be better to translate that into pixels (if it isn't already) and use that at the DisplayServer level. I think that's the intended unit for `InputEventPanGesture`.

Regarding Wayland, I'm not sure if the current implementation uses pixels but if not I can probably fix that. I'll take a look while I'm at it.

Update: It uses surface-local pixels (i.e. unscaled pixels). I think I should scale them.

Anyways, I kinda wonder why everything is divided by 8. Maybe it was meant to be used as fractions of a scrollwheel?

Edit2: To be clear, IMO we should use pixels as the intended unit and adapt to that if it isn't. According to the Apple docs, the MacOS backend is already returning points (device-independent pixels, I think), which are pretty close to that.

> But in case of Android and Wayland it is oversensitive (even more with #116516).

I'm not surprised – as this replaced the existing behaviour. 

We need a way to distinguish the platform. There is an argument for simple and just use `MACOS_ENABLED`, which is arguably no different from actual runtime conditional logic (but more efficient).

Tested, can confirm that it works better on mac now

@stuartcarnie What's your opinion on panning and orbiting sensitivity? (https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/8559, https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/107358)

> What's your opinion on panning and orbiting sensitivity? ([godotengine/godot-proposals#8559](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/8559), #107358)

@passivestar I read that proposal, and I agree that it is too low. We have competing tensions between the platforms that try to unify the events, but they work differently. I did some reading on Windows and Linux trackpad events vary. Linux is even more complicated as different window managers and input systems will also affect how input events from a trackpad are produced 😭

> I do wonder why this PR negates the 0.03 factor for MacOS trackpad deltas by adding a factor of 32, rather than removing both factors altogether. Removing them could potentially fix the issues with Linux, very similar to my attempted Linux solution in #116516, although I did find while testing my PR that Linux needed an additional factor of about 5 to feel like the scrolling speed was consistent with other applications--I'm unsure why.

@GalaxyShard you are correct – we shouldn't be applying / undoing these factors. This PR was mostly an experiment for other macOS user's to try and see if scrolling felt more natural. I'm encouraged that Linux may be similar to macOS, as it might mean we can generalise the solution. Perhaps it's a feature returned by the `DisplayServer`, so that controls can handle the events accordingly?

@stuartcarnie I'm currently working on a similar PR. I intend to introduce a new enum (`InputEventPanGesture::DeltaUnit`) and a new property (`InputEventPanGesture::delta_unit`) which can either be `InputEventPanGesture::DeltaUnit::DELTA_UNIT_LINE` or `InputEventPanGesture::DeltaUnit::DELTA_UNIT_PIXEL`.

I think it's important to distinguish both types of input, as pan gesture can be both (from what I learned when I search for the way Wayland handles that. (cc. @GalaxyShard @deralmas)

You can see my work so far [on my fork branch](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/compare/master...adamscott:godot:support-for-precise-pan-gesture). (feel free to pick whatever you see)

In fact, the whole pan gesture is kinda a mess throughout the engine. Sometimes, it's based on a percentage of the container, sometimes it behaves as reading pixels, and others, it behaves as reading line scrolls.

We should really announce which unit is used when, so users could be able to treat the values as they need to be treated.

Makes me think that we should also advertise the scrolling axis, if it's treated as "normal" or "natural" (i.e. Apple reversed). That's because people could adapt their UI based on that.
@adamscott that is fantastic, and makes sense, so that the control can adapt presentation based on the pan gesture data.

And to note, my experimentation was just to explore whether we could get a natural macOS feel for the controls, and this PR proves that. You solution is going down the correct path for supporting all platforms 👏🏻

> I think it's important to distinguish both types of input, as pan gesture can be both (from what I learned when I search for the way Wayland handles that. (cc. @GalaxyShard @deralmas)

This makes sense.

> Makes me think that we should also advertise the scrolling axis, if it's treated as "normal" or "natural" (i.e. Apple reversed). That's because people could adapt their UI based on that.

Not sure if this will be reliable. macOS handle it half broken way (mode is set for all devices, instead of trackpad only), and there are a bunch of third-party apps to change it for trackpad and mouse independently (which are likely doing in a hacky way).

> Not sure if this will be reliable. macOS handle it half broken way (mode is set for all devices, instead of trackpad only), and there are a bunch of third-party apps to change it for trackpad and mouse independently (which are likely doing in a hacky way).

From what I understand, [its a property from `NSEvent`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nsevent/isdirectioninvertedfromdevice?language=objc). The `[event directionInvertedFromDevice]` property returns a boolean if the direction was inverted by the OS. We could just expose this property (there's an equivalent for Wayland from what I saw) without touching the data itself.

> I think it's important to distinguish both types of input, as pan gesture can be both

On the internal side of things it should certainly be distinguished; right now it seems the engine doesn't account for OS-level implementation details like what kind of units of pixels are used, hence the issues with Linux/Wayland and MacOS. However, once the OS-specific input handling code finishes pushing out the pan gesture events. I think it should be standardised across all platforms and not behave differently so we don't run into the same Linux-MacOS inconsistencies we have now.

> In fact, the whole pan gesture is kinda a mess throughout the engine. Sometimes, it's based on a percentage of the container, sometimes it behaves as reading pixels, and others, it behaves as reading line scrolls.

As of when I created my PR for fixing Linux gestures (~~some MacOS code has changed since then, so I'm not certain if this is still the case~~ edit: this code is unchanged), the pan gesture events always output some unit of pixels (whether physical or logical/screen-scaled, or something else I haven't found in any documentation), but for some reason it's being used in these three different ways. I imagine it could simply have been caused by a developer mixing up handling of pan events and mouse scroll events, or odd input handling quirks of windows mistakenly applied to the Linux/MacOS code.

> Makes me think that we should also advertise the scrolling axis, if it's treated as "normal" or "natural" (i.e. Apple reversed). That's because people could adapt their UI based on that.

From a user perspective I think this would cause more issues than improvements, for example, when dealing with multiple input devices (mouse+touchpad), and I imagine more than one developer will think they have to manually invert the pan deltas to account for the scroll direction (which result in the scroll direction being the same regardless of the user's preference).

Edit:

When creating my PR I found a few things that may be relevant to this PR (cc @adamscotts)

It may be helpful to know that Windows does not use pan events at all.

Linux, as I mentioned earlier, always outputs the number of pixels (based on testing, logical pixels / the real number of pixels but then scaled by the screen scaling factor).

MacOS is a bit odd. See code:

```cpp
if ([event phase] != NSEventPhaseNone || [event momentumPhase] != NSEventPhaseNone) {
	[self processPanEvent:event dx:delta_x dy:delta_y];
}
```

This is the only situation in which pan events are emitted on MacOS. This appears to come from https://stackoverflow.com/a/13981577, and the purpose is to only emit pan events for touchpad input and not any kind of mouse input. Touchpads should always give precise, pixel deltas when scrolling, not full-line scrolls like a mouse wheel might. Thus, pan events are only ever emitted with pixel values.

> On the engine-internal side of things it should certainly be distinguished between; right now it seems the engine doesn't account for OS-level implementation details like what kind of units of pixels are used, hence the issues with Linux/Wayland and MacOS.

_The engine_ does though, as in, there are different places for the two units of measure (mouse wheel detent vs gesture pixels). That said _the editor_ and various UI elements don't take this into consideration and the APIs aren't exactly intuitive.

> > On the engine-internal side of things it should certainly be distinguished between; right now it seems the engine doesn't account for OS-level implementation details like what kind of units of pixels are used, hence the issues with Linux/Wayland and MacOS.
> 
> _The engine_ does though, as in, there are different places for the two units of measure (mouse wheel detent vs gesture pixels). That said _the editor_ and various UI elements don't take this into consideration and the APIs aren't exactly intuitive.

To clarify, I meant by this that the OS-specific input handling code should make sure that the scrolling deltas for pan events (mouse wheels aside because they have their own events and I'm not aware of any bugs in that code) are standardised and have a clearly defined unit of measurement before pushing them to the event system. This way the editor and various UI elements would not need to take these implementation details into consideration at all, and could simply use the delta values as given without weird workarounds like arbitrarily scaling the deltas in some cases and not in others.

> However, once the OS-specific input handling code finishes pushing out the pan gesture events. I think it should be standardised across all platforms and not behave differently so we don't run into the same Linux-MacOS inconsistencies we have now.

I don't agree, and I'll go even further. We should deprecate `InputEventMouseButton.factor` (i.e. announce that it will change, but keep the functionality as is) and instead trigger a vertical (or horizontal) only `InputEventPanGesture` to handle scrolling.

And mouse scrolling would have the delta set with a `LINE` (or `COARSE`) setting.

With that, it would be super easy then to port every `InputMouseEventButton` that looks to factor in order to scroll and convert it to a `InputEventPanGesture` (`COARSE`) handler.

> so we don't run into the same Linux-MacOS inconsistencies we have now.

The problem is that technically, macOS could have a touchpad based input that is line based. I ordered last week a generic touchpad that I should receive today. I'm curious, but I'm pretty sure that the "is precise" flag will be false and the units sent by the OS from the touchpad will be line based. So, I'm convinced that it's not a macOS vs Linux difference.

> We should deprecate InputEventMouseButton.factor (i.e. announce that it will change, but keep the functionality as is) and instead trigger a vertical (or horizontal) only InputEventPanGesture to handle scrolling.

I wonder though, what about games with very coarse scrollwheel input (e.g. hotbar/weapon selection) with a "fine" touchpad? Would that require extra logic? Is that an issue already???

It would be nice to somehow receive *both* events and somehow prefer one or the another if capable. That said I might be forgetting some crucial detail.

> > However, once the OS-specific input handling code finishes pushing out the pan gesture events. I think it should be standardised across all platforms and not behave differently so we don't run into the same Linux-MacOS inconsistencies we have now.
> 
> I don't agree, and I'll go even further. We should deprecate `InputEventMouseButton.factor` (i.e. announce that it will change, but keep the functionality as is) and instead trigger a vertical (or horizontal) only `InputEventPanGesture` to handle scrolling.
> 
> And mouse scrolling would have the delta set with a `LINE` (or `COARSE`) setting.
> 
> With that, it would be super easy then to port every `InputMouseEventButton` that looks to factor in order to scroll and convert it to a `InputEventPanGesture` (`COARSE`) handler.

Just to clarify, you are suggesting to use pan gesture events for mouse scrolling instead of the scroll wheel events? I don't think that's a bad idea at all, although it would require a fairly large number of changes and would increase the scope of this issue to impact all platforms and I believe it would also necessitate introducing breaking changes for users.

In my opinion, this could be done as a separate PR, that way the long-standing issue for Linux can be fixed right away and MacOS users won't get a broken 4.8 update.

> The problem is that technically, macOS could have a touchpad based input that is line based. I ordered last week a generic touchpad that I should receive today. I'm curious, but I'm pretty sure that the "is precise" flag will be false and the units sent by the OS from the touchpad will be line based. So, I'm convinced that it's not a macOS vs Linux difference.

Then we would need to add a couple lines of code in godot_content_view.mm to handle this case, since it seems to assume touchpad==precise scrolling right now. Perhaps we could simply replace the if-statement condition with `if ([event hasPreciseScrollingDeltas])`? If I assume this property determines whether to use line-based or pixel-based scrolling units (it wasn't particularly clear when I last checked the documentation), then this is a very easy fix.

> It would be nice to somehow receive _both_ events and somehow prefer one or the another if capable. That said I might be forgetting some crucial detail.

@deralmas Yes, that's what I meant! Sorry if I wasn't clear enough. The wheel "click" must still trigger a button event, but the concept of a button "factor" is kinda stretching the definition of a button event.

I've been thinking a little bit longer and I'm now suggesting that [we should follow Wayland's lead about how they handle that](https://wayland-book.com/seat/pointer.html#axis-events).

- Deprecate `InputEventMouseButton::factor`
- Deprecate `InputEventPanGesture`
- Create `InputEventAxis` (that both encompasses `InputEventMouseButton::factor` and `InputEventPanGesture`)
  - `InputEventAxis::source` determines whether the input is coming from:
    - a wheel scroll
    - a wheel tilt
    - a continuous motion
    - fingers (could be separate or joined with the previous)
  - (and I even see that Wayland handles discrete stops (i.e. my mouse can still register inbetweens between "clicks")

I currently have a Logitech MX Master 4 a the mouse can do wonders. Especially since the wheel can be toggle between having classic mouse wheel "ticks" and to be completely smooth. I'll try to hack the new [OpenLogi](https://openlogi.org/) drivers to know what happens on the OS side for inputs.
